newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: US corporate group against Iran, Libya sanctions.
newsitem.headline: US corporate group against Iran, Libya sanctions.

text.p: An American corporate group seeking business in Southeast Asia said on Thursday that it opposes U.S. sanctions against foreign firms that invest $40 million or more a year in Iran's or Libya's energy sectors.
Asked about the U.S.-ASEAN Council's stand on the threatened U.S. sanctions, several executives from the 13 U.S. firms involved in the council said they believed in free trade and access to markets.
Malaysian national oil company Petronas faces such sanctions after taking a 30 percent stake in a project to develop two oil and gas fields in Iran.

"The American manufacturing community doesn't see unilateral sanctions of this sort as productive or useful," Howard Lewis, an official with the National Association of Manufacturers and a council member, told a news briefing.
In Malaysia for a three-day tour, the council members are also visiting the Philippines, Indonesia and Singapore to meet with corporate executives and officials about joint ventures.
ASEAN, or the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, groups Brunei, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.
"The U.S. is often perceived, particularly the manufacturing community, as not very oriented to international business and international markets...that just isn't true today," Lewis said.

Companies represented on the trip include plumbing concern Roto-Rooter Corp, aviation giant United Technologies Corp, automotive care firm Precision Tune, and Bison Gear and Engineering Corp, which makes gear motors.
Executives said each U.S. company expects to meet eight to 10 Malaysian companies and that the group had met the Malaysian Industrial Development Authority on Thursday.

Arvid Pedersen, director of Asia-Pacific corporate purchasing for United Technologies' international division, said his executives have been talking with national carrier Malaysian Airline System Bhd about a possible joint venture on overhaul and repair centres.
He said no agreements have been signed.
